newsitem.title: UK: Vnesh vulnerable, Russia debt restructing fine-DMG.
newsitem.headline: Vnesh vulnerable, Russia debt restructing fine-DMG.

text.p: Dollar denominated Russian Vneshekonombank debt could fall sharply to 50-55 percent of face value if President Boris Yeltsin dies, but the country's debt restructuring remains intact, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said.
"In the unfortunate (but certainly not impossible) event that Yeltsin dies, Russian debt prices will fall, probably to 50-55," analyst Stuart Parkinson said in a research note.

Dollar Vnesh hit an alltime high of 70 percent of face value last week, but news that Yeltsin's health problems are worse than anticipated, hit the paper which is now bid at 66 3/4 having been as low as 63 1/2 on Tuesday.
Parkinson said that Vnesh remains supported at 62-63 in the short term and whatever happens to Yeltsin is unlikely to derail Russia's debt restructuring.
"The Russian authorities have already announced that they have received a critical mass of acceptances, and the reconciliation process is getting under way," he said.
This leaves room for investors to buy physical loans and sell the when-and-if's against them. -- David Chance London newsroom 44 171 542 5887
